summary: Focused third verification of revision 3 of the knee-edge OOD draft: resolution of round-2 items, changed-rule logic, skeptic, critic

packed.verdict: Revision 3 resolves both high items from the r2 digest, and the core statistics and provenance check out. On item 1, Stage 2 now has its own branch_native_seed and branch_aux_seed, a minibatch-digest assertion, and the Stage 1 branch is re-evaluated on the Stage 2 bank. This matches runtime.py:224-228. On item 2, the gating fit now uses no point near the knee, and q1' = s_edge + 1.2 q2 and the pi0 algebra are correct. I copied random_control_mc.py to scratch and re-ran it; the output is byte-identical to the saved file (sha256 2dc0c383…f716). All eight Part 11 hashes match the files on disk. Every 4.7(ii) bound, both shares, P(g>=1.0) = 0.078, 17.3% and the calibration figure 47.5 ± 5.0 [18, 77] match that output. I also reproduced the R1 operating characteristics (null pass 0.05-0.09, power 0.33-0.40) and R3's (0.85 at zero cost, 0.50 at -3). Several things still keep revision 3 from sealing, though none of them is high. (1) The rescaled V0(b) bar of 0.3 x rho_hat(s05) only absorbs kink rounding up to a width of about 0.028. The protocol's own justification cites widths of 0.02-0.05, and at 0.05 the KC/rho ratio is 0.38. The new F05 early warning uses an absolute 0.25 that is not tied to this bar, so item 5 is only partly fixed. (2) The edit introduced a defect in the Part 9 tables: Review 2's rows 22-23 now sit under Review 3's table, and Review 2's row 1 still describes the four-point fit that revision 3 rejects. (3) A few numbers went stale when the Monte Carlo was re-run (Part 3.7 still says 28,339 ± 289; the output gives 28,347 ± 284). (4) The remaining items are small wording and scope leftovers: Part 6.1 still says "exact rule"; "valid anchor" is used in two senses; V0-S2 makes all of Stage 2 INCONCLUSIVE on a check known before A5; "count mismatch" still routes to INCOMPLETE; the R0 E1 starts have no named stream; there is no K3b reading; and the AUROC step size is wrong. These are low-cost text fixes, plus one choice of V0(b) coefficient to make before A1.

low_findings.section: Part 0 valid anchor (:52), L2 items 1-4 (:183-184), V0(c) (:568), Stage 1 probes (:547)
low_findings.claim: 'Valid anchor' now has two meanings. Part 0's execution-validity definition also catches the reported-only probes at the actor's own a1..a3, so a reported-only probe can remove an anchor from the gated set.
low_findings.evidence: Part 0 defines a valid anchor as one where 'every forced probe executed within the box, no a1..a3 value passed the knee, and every Q^pi computation completed'. L2 uses 'valid anchors' to mean anchors where every predictor passes item 5 (:183-184). V0(c), 'at least 32 valid gated anchors per arm', does not say which meaning applies. Revision 3 moved the gated KC to a1..a3 = 0 and deleted r2's rule '(probes whose a1..a3 pass the knee are excluded and counted)'. The reported second set at the actor's own a1..a3 can pass the knee, and under Part 0 that invalidates the whole anchor.

low_findings.claim: V0-S2 makes all of Stage 2 INCONCLUSIVE on no-stall adequacy. Only R3 needs that check, and its result is known at the end of Stage 1, so it would be learned only after 36 branches have trained. No adequacy check exists for the Stage 2 stall replicate, which is R1's comparator.
low_findings.evidence: :562 says the no-stall runs' adequacy 'gates Stage 2's R3'. :632 makes it a Stage 2-wide INCONCLUSIVE. A non-learning stall replicate would push J(rep, C) down and inflate G in R1, and nothing checks for that, because damage reproduction (:633) is reported only.
low_findings.fix: Evaluate the no-stall adequacy before A5, as a precondition for requesting Stage 2, or scope it to R3 alone ('R3 not computed'). Add a 20k J_E1 adequacy floor for every Stage 2 replicate and BCA branch in stall C and stall R.

low_findings.section: Stage 2 ties (:622); step 0.3 points and gating model (:463, :477)
low_findings.claim: Three small numeric and wording errors were introduced: the AUROC step size, two point labels in G0.5, and the description of the three-point fit.
low_findings.evidence: (a) With ties counted as 0.5, one OOD slot against five in-support slots gives per-anchor AUROC values in steps of 0.1, not 0.2. (b) G0.5 lists '-0.6' as a raw value; float32(-0.6) is -0.60000002. It also lists '-0.72499999' as a 'float32-executed value', but float32(T15(s05)) is -0.72500002, the same as the near-edge slot. -0.72499999 is the float64 T-image (I computed -0.7249999940). (c) The least-squares slope through {-0.5, -0.6, -0.69999999} gives the middle point zero weight, so the fit equals (Q(-0.5) - Q(-0.69999999))/0.2 with sd 7.07 sigma. The '-0.6' point and 'taken at -0.6' are descriptive only.
low_findings.fix: Change 0.2 to 0.1. Use the slot names -0.60000002 and -0.72500002 (and note that T15(s05) rounds to it). Describe s_edge as the two-point secant, and state its 7.07 sigma noise next to the 25.4 sigma it replaces.

verified.section: Stage 1 V0(b) (DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:565), L2 link (:194), step 0.3 G0.5 F05 and label table (:468, :493)
verified.claim: Digest item 5 is only partly resolved. The new relative bar, |median KC_s05(R)| <= 0.3 x median rho_hat(s05), still fails a correctly labelled RANDOM critic whose kink rounding is wider than about 0.028. The text's own justification cites a range of 0.02-0.05. The F05 early warning uses an absolute 0.25 that is not tied to the relative bar.
verified.evidence: Take a kink that changes the slope by Δs and is rounded with a softplus of width w. Then KC_s05 = Δs[0.05 - sp_w(0.05) + sp_w(0)] and rho(s05) = 0.05 Δs, so KC/rho does not depend on Δs. I computed KC/rho = 0.137 at w=0.01, 0.246 at w=0.02, 0.312 at w=0.03, 0.353 at w=0.04 and 0.380 at w=0.05. Line 194 still says a critic that 'rounds the slope-3 kink over 0.02-0.05 still shows KC_s05 of about 0.2-0.5'. Its own upper half lies above 0.3 x rho, so Stage 1 can still end INCONCLUSIVE whatever the hypothesis. F05 measures the same rounding at stall_slope 1.5, where the slope change is 2.5 against 4 at slope 3. F05 is flagged at an absolute 0.25, and neither the relative bar nor that slope ratio enters the flag.
verified.fix: Choose a coefficient that covers the rounding width you consider plausible: about 0.4 covers w <= 0.05, and the K1a margin still holds, because 0.6 x rho_hat >= 0.5 needs rho_hat >= 0.83. Alternatively, keep 0.3 and change line 194 to say it covers w <= ~0.03 only. Express the G0.5 flag in relative form, for example median F05 / rho15_hat(s05) > 0.3, or rescale it by 4/2.5. Add the residual risk to Part 8.2.

check.reason: I could not refute it. Revision 3 adopted the digest's example coefficient of 0.3 as written. Its own justification at DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:194 claims the bar covers rounding widths of 0.02-0.05, but 0.3 only covers widths up to about 0.028. The text's own absolute figure (KC_s05 about 0.2-0.5) can only be reproduced with the softplus-width reading the finding uses. A full-transition-width reading would give KC well under 0.1, so the alternative interpretation does not rescue the line. Using the minimum over predictors for rho_hat (:172, :179) can only shrink rho_hat, which makes KC/rho_hat larger, not smaller. The F05 flag (:468, :493) does surface the risk before collection and requires the user's acknowledgement at A3. That mitigates the risk somewhat, but the flag is an absolute 0.25 measured at stall_slope 1.5, so it is not tied to the relative bar. Part 8 (:712) attributes a V0(b) INCONCLUSIVE only to fold non-transfer and never to kink rounding. The consequence is a wasted or uninformative Stage 1 (INCONCLUSIVE whatever the hypothesis), not a false PASS, so medium is right and high is not.
check.evidence: I recomputed KC/rho = [0.05 - sp_w(0.05) + sp_w(0)]/0.05 with sp_w(x) = w ln(1+e^(x/w)): w=0.01 gives 0.137, 0.02 gives 0.246, 0.028 gives 0.301, 0.03 gives 0.312, 0.04 gives 0.353, 0.05 gives 0.380. The ratio does not depend on the slope change. Line 447 gives median rho near s10 of 2.12-2.58. A linear gap then implies rho(s05) of about 1.1-1.3, and rounding widths of 0.02-0.05 give KC of about 0.28-0.49. That matches the text's '0.2-0.5' at :194 and exceeds the 0.3 x rho bar (about 0.33-0.39) once w > 0.028. V0(b) at :565 is '|median KC_s05(RANDOM)| <= 0.3 x median rho_hat(s05)'. The G0.5 flag at :493 is 'median F05 > 0.25', absolute, at stall_slope 1.5, where the thrust-slope change is 2.5 (T15(s05) = -0.725 = -KNEE + 1.5 x 0.05), against 4 at slope 3. The flag is not scaled to the relative bar. Digest r2 item 5 offered 0.3 only as an example. Part 9 row 5 (:801) marks the item resolved. Part 8 (:703-732) has no residual-risk entry for kink rounding at V0(b).

packed.verdict: Revision 3 fixes most of what changed correctly. The step 0.3 gating algebra is right: q1' = s_edge + 1.2 q2 is the linear coefficient for slope s_edge at -0.6, and pi0 = (m + 2 lambda' q1')/(1 - 4 lambda' q2) follows from the td3_bc.py actor loss, whose BC term is a mean over 4 dimensions, giving the factor 2 lambda. The model is well conditioned. On the saved five-slot Q1 values it reproduces the step 0.1 forecast (0.562-0.781 per cell) with forecast SD 0.01-0.03. A cell fails only if the edge slope is 3.6-5.3 units flatter than the five-slot quadratic implies, so the conflict with G0.5 is largely gone. Other changes are correct: the seed separation, the verbatim calibration rule, the INCOMPLETE/INCONCLUSIVE split with matching 6 SD bounds and hashes, the R0 adequacy floor, the stated operating characteristics of R1 and R3, and the no-re-attempt and recording rules. Four of the changes do not achieve what they claim. (1) The new onset error F05 cannot see the kink rounding that V0(b) bounds. Rounding inflates KC_s05 through the -KNEE reference. F05 instead compares s05 with T15(s05) = -0.725, where the rounding error is almost the same, so F05/rho is about 0 to -0.11, and the one-sided flag at 0.25 never fires. (2) The scaled V0(b) bar still fails a correctly labelled critic once the rounding width exceeds about 0.03 (softplus model) or 0.045 (Gaussian model), which is most of the 0.02-0.05 range the text itself cites. Its rho_hat comes from a continuation no gate checks. (3) R3's difference-in-differences uses RANDOM as the control. At high load RANDOM has almost no labels in R_deep- (about 18 rows), so the subtraction can also remove most of the knee-specific cost of caution that R3 is meant to catch. (4) The operating characteristics of PROMISING are stated for R1 alone. With R2 and R3 included, power at a true +3 benefit is about 0.05-0.28, not about a third. Smaller problems: the step 0.3 points are computed at mixed a1..a3 values. The second-identical-INCOMPLETE rule is ambiguous next to the fix-then-retry remedies. V0-S2 should be checked before A5. The minibatch digest has no Stage 1 counterpart. The readings and the NOT-PROMISING-consistent definition have gaps. Some wording is left over from revision 2. None of these items requires redesigning the condition, but items 1-4 change gate logic or what the protocol tells the reader and should be fixed before sealing at A1.

low_findings.section: Step 0.3 forward passes and gating model (:463, :475-479)
low_findings.claim: The gating model combines s_edge and q2 measured at different a1..a3 settings. The saved five-slot Q1 values were computed with a1..a3 = 0. The new eight points use 'a1..a3 at each row's saved values' (and G0.5 uses 0). The equilibrium being forecast is the actor's a0 at its own a1..a3.
low_findings.evidence: rerun1 per_probe.actions: slot 0 is the actor's action with nonzero a1..a3; slots 1-5 are [-0.5|-0.25|0|0.25|0.5, 0, 0, 0]. For probes, a 'saved value' is therefore ambiguous (0 or the actor's own), while visited rows get all 13 points at the actor's a1..a3. Any a0 x a1..a3 interaction in the critic makes the two q2 values differ. The five slots also overlap the old hole region (|a0| <= 0.25 at high load) for the hole cells. Hole/s1 has q2 median +0.05 with range [-3.39, +3.42], against medians of -0.6 to -1.1 elsewhere.
low_findings.fix: Evaluate all 13 points at one convention, preferably the actor's own a1..a3 since that is what the forecast concerns, and refit q2 on the five slots at that convention. This is about 5 x 32 forward passes per cell, well inside the cap. Report the a1..a3 = 0 version as descriptive.

low_findings.section: 5.0 rerun rules (:421-422) vs step 0.2 (:456) and step 0.3 (:491)
low_findings.claim: The new second-identical-INCOMPLETE rule is ambiguous next to the fix-then-retry remedies. If the rerun is not preceded by a fix, a deterministic plumbing bug becomes a terminal INCONCLUSIVE that 'cannot be re-attempted under the same design', ending the design over a code defect. If a fix is allowed, a failure is never 'identical'. 'Identically' is undefined for wall-clock caps.
low_findings.evidence: Line 421 requires a rerun 'with identical seeds and streams' and makes a second identical failure INCONCLUSIVE. Line 456 says INCOMPLETE 'blocks every later approval until fixed'; line 491 says 'Fix the evaluator, then a fresh A2'. Line 422 forbids any re-attempt after INCONCLUSIVE. At step 0.4, a count mismatch found after collection would need a mask-builder fix made after the data exist, and no rule says whether that is permitted.
low_findings.fix: State that an INCOMPLETE may be followed by a code-only fix (seeds, thresholds, data and design untouched) with the diff recorded and approved. Apply the second-failure rule only to reruns with unchanged code, that is, nondeterministic units and caps. Define 'identically' (same unit, same check, same failure value or cap).

low_findings.claim: V0-S2 depends only on Stage 1 data, the no-stall runs' 20k J_E1 gain, yet it is evaluated after the 36 Stage 2 branches (about 5 h). It also voids R1 and R2, although only R3 needs it.
low_findings.evidence: Stage 1 V0 explicitly excludes the no-stall-trained runs ('reported here and gates Stage 2's R3'). Stage 1 can therefore PASS, A5 can be approved and trained, and the result is a certain INCONCLUSIVE.
low_findings.fix: Check the no-stall adequacy floor before requesting A5. If it fails, either stop before training or mark R3 'not computed (guard)' and rule PROMISING unavailable, rather than labelling all of Stage 2 INCONCLUSIVE after training.

low_findings.section: Stage 2 seeds and minibatch digest (:612-616, :631); recovery LCB rationale (:647)
low_findings.claim: The minibatch-digest assertion has nothing to compare against. The prior pipeline records no such digest, and Stage 1's assertions do not require one. Separately, revision 3's reason for declining a noise estimate ('no per-fork noise estimate exists') no longer holds once the seeds are separated.
low_findings.evidence: train_worker.py:307 rebuilds the phase-0 sampled indices only into a 'seen' ledger, with no digest. runtime.py branch() looks seeds up per seed index, protocol['seeds'][seed_index] (:223-225), whereas revision 3 asks for seeds 'per fork'. After separation, the Stage 1 native branch re-evaluated on the Stage 2 bank is a second, independent native draw from each of the 12 forks. It was selected through the Stage 1 PASS, but J(rep) - J(Stage 1 native) still gives an empirical branch-noise scale with which to check the 3.55 assumption behind the R1 and R3 operating characteristics.
low_findings.fix: Require Stage 1 branches to record a minibatch-index digest (phase-0 index arrays in order, sha256) under the same definition. Specify how per-fork seeds map onto the reused per-seed-index lookup. Report the 12 rep-minus-Stage-1 differences as a check of the noise assumed in the operating characteristics, with the selection caveat.

low_findings.claim: The ordered readings leave out K3b, and they say nothing for the case where an earlier criterion fails in some seeds but not all. The new NOT-PROMISING-consistent label applies whenever a pooled clause fails, even when one outlier seed drives the failure, or when chance does: R3 fails 15% of the time at zero cost.
low_findings.evidence: The list runs K1c, K1a, K2, K3a, K3c. If K3b is the first criterion to fail in every seed, no rule applies. If K1a fails in two seeds and K2 in all three, K2 governs, but reading 3's precondition ('K1 passes' in every seed) is unmet and the text does not say that no reading follows. On G = (+10, +8, -12), R1's mean of 2 fails, which is labelled 'consistent' although the sign clause is mixed. That differs from Stage 1, where 'consistent' means the same failure in all seeds.
low_findings.fix: Insert K3b into the order (or state that it carries no reading). Add 'if the governing reading's precondition fails, no reading is attached'. Define NOT-PROMISING-consistent for pooled clauses as the pooled clause failing and also failing per seed in all three seeds; otherwise label it mixed.

low_findings.claim: Wording and number leftovers in the revision 3 text.

critic.verdict: Revision 3 correctly resolves both high items from the r2 digest. Stage 2 now has its own seeds, and the gating forecast no longer uses points near the knee. No high-severity item remains, but two medium items are still open and each needs a decision about gate logic before sealing. (1) R3's difference-in-differences uses no-stall RANDOM as its control. At high load RANDOM has almost no labels in R_deep- (about 18.5 rows, against 1,105 at low load), so the subtraction cancels most of the deep-region cost of caution that R3 is named for. As written, H measures cost mainly in the onset band. (2) The V0(b) bar of 0.3 x rho_hat(s05) covers kink rounding only up to a width of about 0.028 (softplus) or 0.045 (Gaussian). It compares two points that are both off the kink, so under rounding F05/rho is about 0 to -0.11, while the flag is one-sided at +0.25. The rest is low-severity bookkeeping: misplaced Part 9 rows, stale Monte Carlo figures, Part 6.1's 'exact rule', the double meaning of 'valid anchor', V0-S2's timing and scope, INCOMPLETE rerun semantics, the missing K3b reading, PROMISING's joint power, the a1..a3 convention in step 0.3, the minibatch digest with nothing to compare against, the unnamed R0 E1 stream, and the AUROC step size. residual_risks: Even with R3 repaired, Stage 2 is a weak screen. With all three PROMISING clauses together, power to detect a true +3 benefit is roughly 5-30% depending on how good the distance arm is, so NOT-PROMISING is weak evidence against BCA.

If R3 keeps no-stall RANDOM as its control, BCA can be called PROMISING while being needlessly cautious at high-load depth, where going deep actually helps. The control is almost as blind there as CUTOFF.

Stage 1 can end INCONCLUSIVE for a reason unrelated to the hypothesis: a correctly labelled RANDOM critic that merely smooths the kink at the knee over more than about 0.03 fails V0(b). Until F05 is replaced, nothing before collection will warn of this.

The pre-collection forecast in step 0.3 relies on a quadratic fit fitted away from the knee. A sharply rounded or oddly curved critic near the edge could still make the forecast miss, and it combines measurements taken at different a1..a3 settings.
A Stage 2 replicate or BCA branch that fails to learn would distort the R1 comparison, and no adequacy check catches it.
The noise level (SD about 3.55) behind every stated pass probability comes from earlier same-fork proxies and is not re-checked on this design's own branches.

The INCOMPLETE rerun rules leave open whether a code fix is allowed. A deterministic plumbing bug could end the whole design as INCONCLUSIVE, or a fix could be applied after data exist without a clear approval path.

The remaining low items (misplaced review rows, stale figures, two meanings of 'valid anchor', unnamed seed streams) are each small, but together they make it easier to misread which rule applies at execution time.
